description: A suspicious service has been detected on the target host. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential ELF_IMEIJ backdoor threat. The malware is known to exploit CGI vulnerabilities to download and execute malicious payloads. Your goal is to identify, contain, and eradicate the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: A suspicious service has been detected on the target host. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential ELF_IMEIJ backdoor threat. The malware is known to exploit CGI vulnerabilities to download and execute malicious payloads. Your goal is to identify, contain, and eradicate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target host, you noticed an unusual service running. Investigate the running services on the target host and identify any suspicious or unauthorized services.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is likely to have an unusual name or configuration. Look for services that do not match the standard system services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. Investigate the persistence mechanisms used by the service.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, you can examine the systemd service files and timers. Use the `systemctl list-unit-files` command to list all unit files and look for any related to the suspicious service. The hidden flag is the name of the persistence mechanism or identifier.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd service files and timers to see how the service is configured to start automatically.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-unit-files` command to list all unit files and look for any related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The persistence mechanism is likely to be a systemd service or timer. Look for any services or timers that are enabled and related to the suspicious service.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control (C2) server. Determine which network port is used for this communication.
levels.solution: To determine the network port used for C2 communication, you can use network monitoring tools to observe the outgoing connections from the target host. Use the `netstat -tuln` command to list all network connections. The hidden flag is the C2 port number.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to observe the outgoing connections from the target host.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `netstat -tuln` command to list all network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The C2 communication is likely to be on an unusual port. Look for any connections to external IP addresses on non-standard ports.
